theme.title: NBA Mix 56
theme.subtitle: Five moments from across NBA history
theme.recap: Five NBA stories, five different numbers: a quick tour of stars, teams, records and surprises.

questions.prompt: The 2009 title was which championship in Lakers history?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Lakers defeated the Magic in five games to win the franchise's 15th NBA championship

funFacts.text: The Lakers' return to the summit came one year after their Finals defeat to rival Boston.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: This was the seventh time in NBA Finals history that a team that lost the championship the previous season has won

funFacts.text: Orlando's only win in the series was its first Finals game victory in franchise history.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Orlando Magic's Game 3 victory was the first win in an NBA Finals game in franchise history

funFacts.text: Los Angeles beat Orlando in a series nicknamed the 'Disney Series' because of the nearby theme parks.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: This series was nicknamed the "Disney Series"

questions.prompt: What was the Warriors' win total at the 2016 All-Star break?
questions.context: Golden State Warriors · 2015–16 · first half of the season
questions.note: 48–4, the best record ever at the break.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Golden State reached the NBA All-Star break at 48–4, the best start to an NBA season at this juncture.

funFacts.text: Klay Thompson beat teammate Stephen Curry in the All-Star weekend Three-Point Contest.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Klay Thompson won the Three-Point Contest at the All-Star weekend, beating Stephen Curry

funFacts.text: Draymond Green had already tied Tom Gola's Warriors record for triple-doubles in one season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Green tied Hall of Famer Tom Gola's franchise record of nine triple-doubles

funFacts.text: Golden State reached fifty wins faster than any NBA team before it had done.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: fastest team to reach 50 wins in a season, accomplishing this in just 55 games

questions.prompt: Facing a sweep in 2017, Cleveland set a Finals record for points in a quarter. How many?
questions.note: 49 in the first quarter of Game 4.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Cleveland scored 49 points in the first quarter, the most points of any period in an NBA Finals game

funFacts.text: Cleveland's Game 4 victory ended Golden State's bid for a completely unbeaten postseason.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Warriors won the first three games, giving them a 15–0 record

funFacts.text: The Warriors–Cavaliers trilogy was the first time the same clubs played three consecutive NBA Finals.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the first time in NBA history that the same two teams played in three consecutive Finals

funFacts.text: Kevin Durant earned the Finals MVP award unanimously after his first championship series with the Warriors.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Kevin Durant was unanimously voted the NBA Finals Most Valuable Player

questions.prompt: How many points per game did Larry Nance average in 1983–84?
questions.context: Phoenix · first Slam Dunk champion · season scoring
questions.note: 17.7 points per game from the athletic forward.

funFacts.text: Nance started all eighty-two Suns games.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Larry Nance | 82 | 82 | 35.4

funFacts.text: His 57.6 percent field-goal accuracy was exceptional.

questions.prompt: On May 9, 2016, Stephen Curry set an NBA record for points in an overtime period. How many did he score?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: He scored 17 of his points in overtime, which broke the NBA record of 16

funFacts.text: Curry returned from an MCL injury absence to score forty points against Portland.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Curry scored 40 points in his first game back after being out injured for 15 days with an MCL sprain

funFacts.text: The previous overtime-period scoring mark belonged to Gilbert Arenas.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: broke the NBA record of 16 held by Gilbert Arenas for most points scored in an overtime period

funFacts.text: The following day, Curry became the NBA's first unanimous regular-season MVP.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Curry is the 11th player to win back-to-back MVP honors and is the first unanimous winner
